anna_ml: Quick follow-up from the bundle-transport hack session — sketching a tighter set of constraints before we commit to a design.

mike_infra: +1. summary please, my brain is full of packaging options rn.

anna_ml: TL;DR: we need a transport format for model bundles that supports (a) partial/streaming load for warmup, (b) atomic install + rollback, (c) efficient delta updates between versions, and (d) cryptographic provenance.

tara_runtime: Important to call out: runtime wants chunk-level KV cache reuse across versions. If we change chunk boundaries we lose all warm cache gains.

sasha: That motivates stable chunking (content-addressed?) so deltas map to identical chunks. But stable chunking makes bundle manifests larger and can complicate encoding for quantized blobs.

lee_sre: From infra side: CDN caching behavior matters a lot. If we have many tiny chunks CDN overhead kills performance. Need an option to serve large ranged objects too.

mike_infra: So we have two knobs: chunk/granularity for dedup/deltas vs large-range-friendly blobs. Can we provide both? e.g., bundle container that exposes a single monolithic object + an index of chunk digests for delta/apply.

anna_ml: That's the idea I sketched: .bundle is opaque tar-like file with an embedded index.json (signed). Index lists chunk offsets + sha256. Client can: a) range-download slices to stream warmup OR b) fetch the whole .bundle for atomic swap.

tara_runtime: Concern: verifying signature while streaming. We need to ensure we don't accept partially-corrupted chunks that later fail verification after we've used them for warmup.

sasha: Two approaches: streaming incremental verification (Merkle-tree over chunks) or fetch signature + small proof then verify each chunk's digest as it arrives. Merkle lets you verify subset quickly.

lee_sre: Merkle is nice but more complex for producers. Also rolling deltas (patches) become Merkle-diff problems. Simpler approach: sign index + chunk digests individually; verify chunk digest on arrival, only add to KV cache after validation.

anna_ml: That aligns with runtime: warmup can optimistic-read but must not commit to cache until verification passes. We can do "speculative warmup" where logits are reserved but not used for final output until commit.

mike_infra: Also need to design server-side APIs: bundle manifest endpoint returns index + version, and a /bundle/{id}/range supports range + conditional GET. For delta updates we can provide /bundle/{id}/delta?from=old -> returns patch file built from chunk diffs.

sasha: Building delta server-side implies storing chunkized history or running on-the-fly chunking. Storage cost increases but patch payloads shrink — good trade for frequently-updated tiny changes (LOTR fine-tuning).

tara_runtime: Another operational concern: warmup heuristics. For models with hot prefixes, streaming the first N layers is useful. If chunk boundaries are layer-aligned we get faster useful warmup.

anna_ml: So add recommendation: canonical chunking strategy is "layer-aware content chunks" for recommended models; fallback to content-defined chunking for others. Document must show how to map layer->chunk mapping.

lee_sre: We should also define atomic swap semantics: download to tmpdir, run verification on all needed metadata (index sig, chunk digests), then move to live path with atomic rename + restart hook. Rollback by keeping previous folder for X minutes by default.

mike_infra: Agreed. Also retention policy for old bundles & delta chain length needs limits (keep last 3 versions default) to bound storage and patch compute cost.

sasha: One more: in-cloud vs private deploy differences — private on-prem may prefer signed artifact bundles pushed via internal registries; hosted can leverage CDN + delta generation. We need two operational modes in spec.

anna_ml: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with: artifact format (bundle + index.json + optional .delta), verification flow (Merkle-lite or chunk-digest), runtime contract (speculative warmup, commit), server APIs, and ops appendix (retention, CDN hints, rollback policy). 

mike_infra: Please include example curl snippets and the minimal index schema.

anna_ml: Example index in thread for prototyping:

```
{
  "bundle_id": "sha256:...",
  "version": "2026-03-18T12:00:00Z",
  "chunks": [
    {"offset": 0, "length": 10485760, "digest": "sha256:aaa...", "layer_range": "0-3"},
    {"offset": 10485760, "length": 8388608, "digest": "sha256:bbb...", "layer_range": "4-7"}
  ],
  "signature": "sig:v1:...",
  "producer": "registry.redwood-internal"
}
```

mike_infra: Nice. For curl: `curl -H \"If-None-Match: \$OLD_ETAG\" -o bundle.part \"$CDN/bundles/sha256:...\"` then `curl -r 0-10485759 -o layer0.chunk \"$CDN/bundles/sha256:...\"` etc.

tara_runtime: I'll prototype a runtime shim that exposes: fetch_index(), stream_chunk(digest, offset, len), verify_chunk(digest), speculative_apply(), commit_swap(). Will post code in a follow-up.

sasha: Cool. If we keep chunk digests stable and layer-aligned, delta generation should be straightforward. We should run a dataset of 50 common models to choose default chunk sizes (balance CDN perf vs delta efficiency).

anna_ml: Action items: 1) anna -> RFC addendum draft (w/ index schema + curl examples) 2) tara -> runtime shim prototype 3) mike -> CDN + delta infra cost estimate 4) sasha -> chunking/experiment on 50 models

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: generate-rfc-draft -> queue job created by anna_ml (id: 2026-03-18-01)

lee_sre: Thanks. Let's keep this thread for follow-ups; please post links to prototypes in the RFC doc.

anna_ml: Will do. Thanks all :rocket:
